subject: english
text: Neither the manager nor the employees ___ present at the meeting.
explanation: With "neither…nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Employees" is plural, so "were".

subject: english
text: The list of items ___ on the table.
explanation: The subject is the singular "list"; "of items" is only a modifier.

subject: english
text: Each of the students ___ given a certificate.
explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes a singular verb.

subject: english
text: A number of students ___ absent today.
explanation: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb. (Compare "The number of students is large".)

subject: english
text: The news ___ surprising.
explanation: "News" looks plural but is an uncountable, singular noun.

subject: english
text: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
explanation: Two past events: the earlier one (leaving) uses the past perfect.

subject: english
text: She ___ in this company since 2019.
explanation: "Since 2019" signals an action continuing up to now: present perfect (continuous).

subject: english
text: I ___ my homework when the power went out.
explanation: An action in progress in the past that was interrupted: past continuous.

subject: english
text: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

subject: english
text: He is ___ honest man.
explanation: "Honest" begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so "an".

subject: english
text: She plays ___ violin very well.
explanation: Musical instruments take "the" when we speak of playing them.

subject: english
text: ___ Sun rises in the east.
explanation: Unique objects (the Sun, the Moon) take "the".

subject: english
text: I have ___ university degree in engineering.
explanation: "University" starts with a "yoo" consonant sound, so "a".

subject: english
text: She is good ___ mathematics.
explanation: The fixed collocation is "good at".

subject: english
text: He was accused ___ stealing the money.
explanation: "Accused of" is the correct collocation.

subject: english
text: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
explanation: "Prefer X to Y" is the standard pattern.

subject: english
text: He is married ___ a doctor.
explanation: "Married to" is correct.

subject: english
text: The meeting has been postponed ___ next Monday.
explanation: "Postponed until" a future date.

subject: english
text: Find the part with an error: "She don't like spicy food."
explanation: A third-person singular subject needs "doesn't": "She doesn't like spicy food."

subject: english
text: Find the part with an error: "Neither of the boys have completed their homework."
explanation: "Neither" is singular, so it should be "has completed".

subject: english
text: Find the part with an error: "He is senior than me by two years."
explanation: "Senior" and "junior" are followed by "to": "senior to me".

subject: english
text: Find the part with an error: "I have been knowing him for ten years."
explanation: Stative verbs like "know" are not used in continuous tenses: "I have known him".

subject: english
text: Find the part with an error: "The furniture in the room are very old."
explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable and takes a singular verb: "is very old".

subject: english
text: Choose the passive form of: "The chef cooked the meal."
options: The chef was cooked by the meal.
The meal is cooked by the chef.
The meal has been cooked by the chef.
The meal was cooked by the chef.
explanation: Simple past active becomes "was/were + past participle".

subject: english
text: Choose the passive form of: "They are building a new bridge."
options: A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.
A new bridge was built by them.
A new bridge is being built by them.
explanation: Present continuous active becomes "is/are being + past participle".

subject: english
text: Choose the passive form of: "Someone has stolen my wallet."
explanation: Present perfect active becomes "has/have been + past participle".

subject: english
text: Choose the active form of: "The report was submitted by Rahul."
explanation: Past passive "was submitted" becomes simple past "submitted".

subject: english
text: Choose the indirect speech: He said, "I am tired."
options: He said that he is tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that I am tired.
He said that he was tired.
explanation: Reporting verb in the past shifts "am" to "was" and "I" to "he".

subject: english
text: Choose the indirect speech: She asked me, "Where do you live?"
options: She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I live?
explanation: In reported questions, use statement word order and shift the tense.

subject: english
text: Choose the indirect speech: The teacher said to the class, "Open your books."
options: The teacher said the class that open your books.
The teacher asked the class if open their books.
The teacher told the class opened their books.
The teacher ordered the class to open their books.
explanation: Imperatives are reported with "ordered/told + to + verb".

subject: english
text: Choose the synonym of ABUNDANT.
explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities.

subject: english
text: Choose the synonym of BRIEF.
explanation: Brief means of short duration or length.

subject: english
text: Choose the synonym of CANDID.
explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward.

subject: english
text: Choose the synonym of METICULOUS.
explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

subject: english
text: Choose the synonym of EPHEMERAL.
explanation: Ephemeral things last only a very short time.

subject: english
text: Choose the antonym of EXPAND.
explanation: To expand is to become larger; to contract is to become smaller.

subject: english
text: Choose the antonym of ANCIENT.
explanation: Ancient means very old; modern is its opposite.

subject: english
text: Choose the antonym of GENEROUS.
explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

subject: english
text: Choose the antonym of VICTORY.
explanation: Victory is winning; defeat is losing.

subject: english
text: What does the idiom "a piece of cake" mean?
explanation: It describes a task that is very easy to do.

subject: english
text: What does "break the ice" mean?
options: Start a conversation in an awkward situation
explanation: To break the ice is to ease initial social tension.

subject: english
text: What does "once in a blue moon" mean?
explanation: A "blue moon" is rare, so the phrase means "very seldom".

subject: english
text: What does "hit the nail on the head" mean?
options: Say or do exactly the right thing
explanation: It means to be exactly right about something.

subject: english
text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He do not know the answer.
He does not knows the answer.
He does not know the answer.
explanation: After "does", the main verb stays in base form: "know".

subject: english
text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Me and him went to the market.
Him and I went to the market.
Me and he went to the market.
He and I went to the market.
explanation: Subject pronouns (he, I) are used as subjects.

subject: english
text: The CEO's speech was so ___ that the entire audience was moved to tears.
explanation: Being moved to tears suggests an emotionally affecting speech.

subject: english
text: Despite his best efforts, the plan ___ because of poor planning.
explanation: "Despite" and "poor planning" point to a negative outcome.

subject: english
text: She has a ___ for languages; she picks them up quickly.
explanation: A "knack for" something means a natural talent for it.

subject: english
text: Arrange in order — P: She opened the door. Q: There was a knock at the door. R: A courier stood outside with a parcel. S: She signed for it and thanked him.
explanation: The knock (Q) comes first, she opens the door (P), sees the courier (R), then signs (S).

subject: english
text: Arrange in order — P: He studied hard for months. Q: Rohan wanted to crack the placement exam. R: He cleared all three rounds. S: Finally, the offer letter arrived.
explanation: Goal (Q), effort (P), result (R), outcome (S).

subject: english
text: Identify the adverb: "She sings beautifully."
explanation: "Beautifully" modifies the verb "sings", so it is an adverb.

subject: english
text: Identify the preposition: "The cat jumped over the fence."
explanation: "Over" shows the relationship between the cat's movement and the fence.

subject: english
text: In "He ran quickly", the word "quickly" is a(n)
explanation: "Quickly" tells how he ran, so it is an adverb.

subject: english
text:
Passage: Remote work has changed how many software teams operate. Without a shared office, teams rely heavily on written communication, documentation and scheduled meetings. Companies report that clear documentation reduces repeated questions and helps new members join faster. However, some managers worry that informal conversations, which often spark ideas, are harder to recreate online. As a result, several teams now set aside short, unstructured video calls just for casual discussion.

What do remote teams rely on heavily?
explanation: The passage says teams rely on written communication, documentation and scheduled meetings.

subject: english
text: An advertisement claims: "Regular use of Brand X toothpaste reduces cavities." Which finding would most weaken this claim?
options: Brand X is the best-selling toothpaste
Brand X users also tend to eat less sugar and visit dentists more often
Brand X costs less than rival brands
Brand X comes in several flavours
explanation: An alternative explanation (diet, dental visits) undermines the causal link. The other options are irrelevant to cavities.

subject: english
text: A company's revenue rose 20% while its headcount stayed the same. Which inference is best supported?
explanation: With revenue up and headcount unchanged, revenue per employee must have risen. The other options need extra information.

subject: english
text: Which is the most appropriate subject line for an email requesting a one-day leave?
explanation: A good subject line is specific and professional.

subject: english
text: Which closing is most appropriate for a formal email to a hiring manager?
explanation: Formal emails end with a polite, professional sign-off.
